parsed.title: Discussion on AI tools, job search automation, and code generation risks

topics.title: Automation of job search and résumé generation

claims.text: User plans to set up OpenClaw for finding vacancies, generating résumés and cover letters.
Full automation with PDF résumé generation is seen as better because recruiters can analyze the document during technical interviews.
Lack of AI‑related skills (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, embeddings) makes job search for JS/Python positions difficult in 2026.

topics.title: Impact of modern AI tools on development speed

claims.text: Acceleration of development became significant only after 2025, despite early ideas appearing around 2022.
Using GPT to generate SQL joins and other code dramatically speeds up routine tasks.
AI‑generated code can introduce performance and security problems, such as overly large raw SQL queries that are slow in production.

topics.title: Critique of AI in recruiting and HR

claims.text: The speaker expects the recruiting profession to become obsolete and sees HR as merely personnel management.
Search for candidates using AI‑related keywords is detached from reality.

topics.title: Concerns about code quality from AI generation

claims.text: Generated code may be inefficient (e.g., SELECT * without approval) and cause production issues.
Incremental computation ideas are being replaced by views, indicating a shift in engineering practice.
Several participants made jokes, sarcasm, or unrelated comments (e.g., about “Ford Mustang”, “strawberries”, or random text).
